summary: This document outlines the Public Safety Officer Suicide Module, detailing various work-related stressors, injury details, and weapon variables associated with PSOs. It also includes appendices that provide guidance on data collection for the National Violent Death Reporting System (NVDRS) and the State Unintentional Drug Overdose Reporting System (SUDORS). The information is crucial for understanding the factors contributing to PSO suicides and improving data reporting practices.

12.4.12 PSOS_WorkRelatedStressors_HR
12.4.13 PSOS_WorkRelatedStressors_retirement
12.4.14 PSOS_WorkRelatedStressors_otherfreetext

Definition: PSOs are exposed to a myriad of work-related stressors that may be chronic and/or acute. The intent of this variable is to capture these stressors. The list of stressors included in the response options is not meant to be exhaustive but rather meant to capture work-related stressors more commonly experienced by PSOs. If there is a stressor that is different from the ones listed, please include it in the “Other” category and specify.

Response Options (Check all that apply):
Homicide of colleague
Suicide of colleague
Witness to serious injury of a colleague
Interpersonal conflict with partner, crew, or other co-worker
Psychological stress of work
Signs or feelings of burnout
Shift-work related stress
Personnel/Human resources issues
Recent/Upcoming retirement
Other (free text)

Discussion: Endorse this variable if, per the source documents, you have evidence that the victim was experiencing a work-related stressor. Work-related stress can come in many forms. Below is a list of definitions for response options that fall under “Work-related stressors.”

Homicide of colleague: Victim experienced the homicide of a work partner/colleague. This response option should be selected regardless of whether the death occurred in the line of duty. The victim is not required to have been a witness to the event.

Suicide of colleague: Victim experienced the suicide of a work partner/colleague. This response option should be selected regardless of whether the death occurred in the line of duty. The victim is not required to have been a witness to the event.

Witness to serious injury of a colleague: Victim witnessed the serious injury to a partner/colleague. This response option should be selected regardless of whether the serious injury occurred in the line of duty.

Interpersonal conflict with partner, crew, or other co-worker: Victim was reported to have experienced stress related to interpersonal conflict with a colleague regardless of whether the conflict occurred on or off duty.

Psychological stress of work: Victim was reported to have psychological stress related to work. Examples include, but are not limited to, traumatic work exposure (e.g., witness to mass casualty event), response to call for a suicide, violence experienced against victim or coworkers, response to a call for a suicidal person, violence toward self or coworkers, responding to a pediatric emergency (fatal and non-fatal), death of a patient or person in custody during or after responding to the scene, or the psychological stress of repeated/constant exposure to trauma.

Signs or feelings of burnout: Victim was reported to have shown signs of or expressed feelings of burnout. Burnout is defined as a syndrome conceptualized as resulting from chronic work-related stress that is usually characterized by three dimensions: feelings of energy depletion or exhaustion, increased mental distance from one's job, or feelings of negativism or cynicism related to one's job, or reduced professional efficiency.

Shift-work related stress: Victim was reported to have experienced stress related to shift work. Examples include, but are not limited to, interrupted sleep, circadian rhythm-related stress, mandatory overtime or holdovers, and shiftwork generally.

Personnel/Human resources issues: Victim was reported to have experienced stress related to personnel/human resources. Examples include, but are not limited to, work-related racism, discrimination, or harassment, poor performance evaluation, being denied or passed over for a promotion, Internal Affairs investigation, or history of disciplinary action at work.

Recent/Upcoming retirement: Victim was reported to have experienced stress related to a recent or upcoming retirement.

Other: Endorse if the victim was reported to have any other work-related stressor that is thought to have contributed to their death. Please fill in the details in the free text box.
12.5 PSOS Injury Detail Variables
12.5.1 Duty status at time of injury: PSOS_DutyStatus
Definition: This variable is meant to capture the duty status of the PSO when the fatal injury occurred.

Response Options:
1. On duty
2. Off duty
66. Other
99. Unknown

Discussion: Endorse “1 – On duty” if the injury occurred while the PSO was working their scheduled shift, overtime, or was called in to work unexpectedly. Endorse “2 – Off duty” if the injury occurred any time outside of the PSO’s scheduled work hours. Endorse “66 – Other” if the PSO was in an on-call status or retired. Examples of “On duty” include any time period where the PSO is dedicating a set number of hours at their workplace. A PSO can be working their shift at any location necessitated by their duties, including dispatch locations and places encountered en route while performing work-related duties.
12.5.2 Decedent affected by chronic or acute work-related injury/disability: PSOS_ChronicAcuteInjuryDisability
Definition: This variable is meant to capture whether the PSO had suffered any work-related injury(ies) or disability(ies).
Response Options: Checkbox

Discussion: Endorse this variable if the decedent suffered and/or was diagnosed with any acute, chronic, or long-term injury or disability while working in the PSO role or due to the work environment. The incidents include, but are not limited to, chronic and acute physical, mental, or neurological injuries or disabilities. For injuries that may have occurred before the PSO’s suicide, only endorse if the injury was thought to have contributed to the suicide. Examples include work-related illnesses or conditions such as: respiratory ailments associated with smoke, burns or corrosion, gunshot wounds, puncture wounds, amputation, concussion, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, emphysema, traumatic brain injury, back injury, post-traumatic stress disorder, anxiety or depressive disorder, traumatic injury to body (e.g., nerves, spinal cord, muscles, bones, ligaments, etc.), and/or other injury/disability.
Detail about where fatal injury occurred

Definition: This variable captures additional details about where the suicide of a PSO occurred.

Response Options (Check all that apply):
Work/Service vehicle
Work site (e.g., firehouse, police department)
Training site (police academy, fire academy)
Military installation/post
Dispatch location (responding to a call)
In the field (includes both dispatched & non-dispatched)
Shooting range
Courthouse
Jail/Corrections facility
Unknown
Other

Discussion: This variable is meant to capture additional information on where the fatal injury occurred that is unique to PSOs and distinct from the variable, “Type of location where injury occurred” in NVDRS. N/A should be used when all relevant injury location information is already captured in the “Type of location where injury occurred” variable on the Injury and Death tab.
12.6 PSOS Weapon Variables
12.6.1 Injury weapon was a work-issued firearm: PSOS_Firearm
Definition: This variable is meant to capture whether the firearm used in the PSO’s death was a service weapon or work-issued weapon.
Response Options: Checkbox

Discussion: Endorse if source documents note that the firearm used to inflict the fatal injury was work-issued. The variable is not restricted to only law enforcement officers. If information is not available regarding whether the firearm was work-issued, do not assume the firearm was work-issued and do not endorse.
13. Appendices

Appendix A is a decision-tree intended to assist states in determining which state enters an incident in the NVDRS web-based system when the incident crosses state lines or a resident was fatally injured in another state. The decision-tree can be used by states collecting statewide data and states with pilot years.

Appendix B includes an overview of the National Violent Death Reporting System (NVDRS) and the State Unintentional Drug Overdose Reporting System (SUDORS). NVDRS uses information from death certificates (DC), coroner/medical examiner (C/ME) reports, and law enforcement (LE) reports to provide a complete picture of violent deaths. The case definition for NVDRS includes homicides, suicides, unintentional firearm deaths, deaths of undetermined intent (including opioid overdose deaths of undetermined intent), deaths due to legal intervention (excluding executions), and deaths due to terrorism. Information from NVDRS can be used to characterize violent deaths and inform, develop, and guide violence prevention programs. SUDORS uses information from DCs and C/ME reports for unintentional drug overdose deaths, and from DCs, C/ME reports, and LE reports for drug overdose deaths of undetermined intent (LE data for drug overdose deaths of undetermined intent are required for NVDRS but not for SUDORS and therefore do not have to be entered by the 8-month SUDORS data entry deadline; see details in table below). The case definition for SUDORS includes drug overdose deaths that are either unintentional or of undetermined intent. Information from SUDORS can be used to characterize drug overdose deaths and inform, develop, and guide overdose prevention programs. Both NVDRS and SUDORS data collection take place using the NVDRS web-based system. SUDORS and NVDRS collect information for different cases, with one exception: drug overdose deaths of undetermined intent. These cases should only be entered once in the web-based system, but within the scope of both SUDORS and NVDRS, and should be coded using abstractor manner of death “9-undetermined intent” and incident type “1-NVDRS” (incident category values of “5-single death of undetermined intent” or “10-multiple deaths of undetermined intent” will be used to identify deaths of undetermined intent from the broader NVDRS incident type) in the web-based system. The content in this document (e.g., data closeout dates, etc.) is for informational purposes only and should not be used as a substitute for the Notice of Funding Opportunity Announcement for either program – SUDORS and NVDRS.

1. Required data fields in web-based system
a. NVDRS cases
i. All data fields are required on all tabs except the Intimate Partner Violence (IPV), Child Fatality Review (CFR), and Overdose (OD) tabs, which are optional.
b. SUDORS cases
i. For unintentional drug overdose deaths:
1. Certain data fields are optional on the Demographics, Injury and Death, and Circumstances tabs.
2. All data fields on the Weapons and Toxicology tabs are required.
3. All but 3 specific data fields on the OD tab are required.
4. Data fields on the Suspects, IPV, and CFR tabs are optional.
ii. For drug overdose deaths of undetermined intent:
1. All data fields are required on the Demographics, Injury and Death, Circumstances, Toxicology, and OD tabs (except 3 specific fields on the OD tab).
2. Data fields on the IPV and CFR tabs are optional.
c. Required fields and Narrative guidance for NVDRS and SUDORS cases are detailed below:

NARRATIVES GUIDANCE
C/ME narrative
Per the NVDRS coding manual guidance, with the following exceptions:
Alternative wording can be used to describe the decedent (i.e., “decedent,” “D”) in addition to “Victim,” “V”
Dates related to the injury, death, and last seen alive can be included in narrative to help verify dates of injury/death/last seen alive
If LE information is available, it should be included in the C/ME narrative

LE narrative
Not required and should be left blank; if LE report is available, information should be captured in the C/ME narrative (i.e., only write one narrative)

Data entry completion
- At minimum, within 8 months of the end of the reporting period†
- SUDORS-required fields only: At minimum, within 8 months of the end of the reporting period for fields required by SUDORS†
- NVDRS-required fields (including LE fields): Within 16 months of the calendar year of death for fields required only by NVDRS

*Only entered once in the web-based system, but within scope of both SUDORS and NVDRS
